rationale: Old English 'Tíw' is the Germanic god of war who was equated with the Roman Mars (hence 'Tuesday' < Tíwesdæg = Mars's day); the gloss explicitly maps Tíw to Mars as a deity, not the planet or the month. The attestations in glossary texts (Wrt. Voc.) confirm this is a mythological/divine identification, matching mars.n.02 (Roman god of war).
